architecture_principles: the unit of decision is an experiment, not a formulation
value of information is computed by a deterministic scientific tool, not by an additional language model
every registered hypothesis carries an explicit pre-result prediction rule and an explicit falsification condition
a measurement that cannot separate any registered hypothesis scores zero discrimination, and that is a scientific result rather than a defect
weight sensitivity is reported as decision stability, never as model confidence
ties in the deterministic layer are reported as ties; the tool must not manufacture a preference it does not have
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
the mechanism question and the Agent framework are separate contributions and are reported separately

candidate_space.rationale: V4 deliberately reuses the byte-identical V3 lattice. Continuous-space optimization and any new wet-lab work are out of scope, so that the measured change between V3 and V4 is the decision object and the VOI layer, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer (including the deterministic VOI tool) -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V4.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime. Its adjudication tests whether a registered hypothesis survives contact with the completed measurement. It is not a contemporaneous pre-experimental record and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_VOI_GUIDED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V4
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
turning the study into a pure AI benchmark
weakening or replacing the rheological mechanism result
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that selects the next formulation x measurement EXPERIMENT by transparent value of information, rather than selecting a formulation candidate alone.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question that the next experiment must answer, then request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations

execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, and the deterministic VOI tool that scores every formulation x measurement experiment card
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value, stating the hypotheses it separates and what each possible outcome would establish
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability of the primary observable, and whether the stated falsification criterion can actually be met by the measurement
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported VOI weight sensitivity and the skeptic's strongest objection
commit to one experiment card, or abstain, and state the acceptance and falsification criteria that will adjudicate it
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card with timestamps, model identifiers and cryptographic hashes of every input

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V4 is an independent architecture. configs/agent_v3.json, prompts/agent_v3_*.txt, src/pur_new/agent_v3.py and every frozen V3 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V4.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards
voi_tool.not_a_posterior: The local design contains six audited realizations and two thermal-hold trajectories. That does not support a calibrated Bayesian expected-information computation, so no posterior probability is fabricated. Weight sensitivity is reported instead.

decision_stability_sent_to_model.metric_is_not: model confidence; posterior probability; calibrated expected information
decision_stability_sent_to_model.tie_interpretation: The deterministic VOI layer is indifferent among the tied top experiments: they share an identical component vector. Tie-breaking is therefore a genuine task left to the Agent, and any selection inside this set cannot have been read off the VOI ranking.
decision_stability_sent_to_model.voi_formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: Accept the result as support for H-RESIN over H-CORE if SI_15_60 is below 3.80% in every independent repeat, with at least two repeats. The 3.80% threshold is one-half of the H-CORE linear-dilution prediction of 7.61% for reactive mass fraction 0.8000.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: Falsify H-RESIN if SI_15_60 is at or above 7.61% in every independent repeat, supporting H-CORE. Conversely, if SI_15_60 is below 3.80% in every independent repeat, falsify H-CORE relative to the registered linear-dilution criterion. Values from 3.80% through 7.60%, or disagreement between repeats across either boundary, do not falsify either hypothesis. This experiment cannot falsify H-RESIN in favor of H-DUAL or distinguish those two hypotheses.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: Run a matched-reactive-mass, controlled-process factorial hold comparison containing the reactive-core condition, 15% acrylic-only condition, 5% tackifier-only condition, and the 15% acrylic plus 5% tackifier condition, using at least three independent preparations per condition and the same M-HOLD-120 protocol.
judge_normalized.primary_observable: SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, reported as percent at 120 C over the matched 15-60 minute window.
judge_normalized.rationale: This card directly measures the established 120 C viscosity-growth failure mode, tests the reactive-core dilution prediction against superlinear suppression, remains within the supported 15% acrylic and 5% minor-tackifier region, and minimizes intervention burden among the deterministic top ties. It is a formulation-level rheological test only and does not establish a molecular mechanism.
judge_normalized.stage_disagreements_resolved: I followed the Proposer and Robustness Adjudicator on selecting S1C41::M-HOLD-120, breaking the genuine five-card tie by choosing the smallest supported modifier burden while directly testing the least-resolved failure coordinate. I followed the Skeptic on interpretation: the dual-axis composition leaves H-RESIN versus H-DUAL entangled, and uncontrolled realization variability makes threshold crossings preliminary unless repeats agree. The Skeptic's objection changes the evidential strength of outcomes but does not make this direct hold experiment scientifically indefensible.

planner.failure_mode: Viscosity growth during prolonged 120 C melt residence, with formulation-dependent thermal-hold drift
planner.failure_mode_evidence: The original 120 C thermal holds show SI_15_60 of 0.095 for E1 versus 0.515 for E5, with SI_15_90 of 0.168 versus 0.931, establishing substantial and formulation-dependent isothermal viscosity growth.
planner.least_resolved_justification: Only E1 and E5 have local 120 C time trajectories, each from a single original run with four points over 15-90 minutes. No acrylic-only or tackifier-containing modified composition has a measured trajectory, and repeatability of the hold drift is unresolved.
measurement_requirements: Measure viscosity at 120 C at 15, 30, 45, and 60 minutes and report the matched-window SI_15_60 relative change.
Use at least two independent preparation repeats so drift differences can be separated from realization variability.
Compare compositions at matched reactive mass fraction, including an acrylic-only condition and a condition with the minor tackifier-like axis active.
Use the same hold temperature, time window, sample history, and reporting units for all compared compositions.
Evaluate the measured drift against both the E1_drift multiplied by reactive mass fraction prediction and the pre-registered superlinear-suppression and tackifier-required predictions.
planner.scientific_question: At matched reactive mass fraction and matched measurement window, does adding the modifier axes reduce 120 C viscosity drift below the reactive-core linear-dilution prediction, and is the low-drift state achievable with the acrylic-like axis alone or only when the minor tackifier-like axis is also active?

hypotheses_not_separated: H-RESIN versus H-DUAL: both predict low drift for this dual-axis composition, so this experiment cannot distinguish them.

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 remains below 3.80% across at least two repeats, the result supports H-RESIN over H-CORE and falsifies the linear-dilution prediction at the stated resolution. Because both modifier axes are active, it does not distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 is at or above 7.61%, H-RESIN is falsified and the result supports the reactive-core linear-dilution account H-CORE; the tackifier-required low-drift prediction of H-DUAL is also not supported for this composition.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A drift between 3.80% and 7.61% is unresolved at the registered decision thresholds: it is not sufficiently low to support H-RESIN over H-CORE, but it is not high enough to falsify H-RESIN by the registered condition. An acrylic-only hold would be required to distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL.

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: It is genuinely tied in deterministic VOI and separates the same hypothesis pairs, but uses a higher acrylic loading without additional discrimination or interpretability benefit.
It is genuinely tied in deterministic VOI and remains within the supported region, but its 20% acrylic loading adds modifier burden without separating any additional registered hypothesis pair.
It is genuinely tied in deterministic VOI, but its 22.5% acrylic loading is a larger intervention than necessary for the same direct drift test and hypothesis separation.
It is genuinely tied in deterministic VOI, but uses the largest acrylic loading in the tied set, increasing intervention burden without improving pairwise discrimination.

proposer.reasoning: The 120 C matched-window hold directly measures the least-resolved coordinate, is interpretable without model fitting or extrapolation, and addresses the established failure mode. S1C41 separates H-CORE from both low-drift alternatives while staying at the minimum supported acrylic level and the central supported tackifier level. Its outcome also clearly defines the required acrylic-only follow-up for resolving H-RESIN versus H-DUAL.
proposer.tie_break_justification: S1C41 uses the smallest supported modifier burden in the tied set: 15% acrylic-like modifier, within the conservative initial acrylic band, plus 5% minor tackifier-like modifier, within the repeatedly documented minor-resin cluster. It retains the same direct hold-drift observability and separates the same two hypothesis pairs as the other tied cards without adding modifier burden.

residual_decision_risk: Uncontrolled process-state variability may obscure or mimic differences in SI_15_60.
The two-repeat protocol does not validate the registered 3.80% and 7.61% decision thresholds.
The dual-axis composition cannot distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL or isolate acrylic, tackifier, and interaction effects.
The tied top set reflects score indifference among five experiments; selecting S1C41 is a scientific minimum-burden tie-break, not an implication of superior VOI.
A stable ranking does not establish that the selected experiment or its hypotheses are scientifically correct.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The strongest objection is that two uncontrolled preparation repeats do not establish the declared 3.80% or 7.61% threshold comparisons in the presence of large 120 C realization variability. It does not make the matched-window 120 C hold a less relevant experiment or change the deterministic top family, but it prevents treating threshold crossings as defensible formulation-mechanism falsification. Results should be interpreted as preliminary drift observations unless process history is controlled, additional independent preparations are used, and a repeat-uncertainty or repeat-agreement rule is applied. The dual-axis composition also leaves H-RESIN versus H-DUAL entangled, so an acrylic-only comparison remains necessary for that attribution.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: The proposal is in the tied top set. No weight perturbation in the 25-scenario sweep changes the tied top set, and every recommendation_flip_boundary reports survival across the full 0.5-1.5 multiplier sweep. These perturbations are scientifically defensible because the experiment directly measures the established failure mode, has high measurement interpretability, and addresses the unresolved isothermal time trajectory. This is decision stability of the transparent score, not model confidence or posterior probability.

skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: The raw SI_15_60 value can be numerically above 7.61% or below 3.80%, but the protocol cannot reliably establish that such a result exceeds the stated 2.00% measurement resolution for the modified composition. Two repeats without process-state controls, repeat agreement requirements, or an uncertainty estimate are insufficient given the observed 120 C realization spread. Thus the criterion is attainable as a numerical outcome but not as a defensible scientific falsification test.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A low-drift result could support a generic resin-modification effect or a tackifier-required effect, but cannot establish that the minor tackifier axis is required or that the acrylic axis is insufficient.
objections.objection: The selected S1C41 composition contains both 15% AC1920 acrylic-like modifier and 5% TK100 minor tackifier-like modifier. Its SI_15_60 predictions for H-RESIN and H-DUAL are identical at 3.804%, so the experiment cannot distinguish those hypotheses. The Proposer explicitly declares this entanglement, but the central question of whether low drift is achievable with the acrylic axis alone remains unanswered.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Mechanism attribution beyond 'this dual-axis formulation differs from the dilution prediction' would be unsupported, including the claim that the tackifier is required or that acrylic addition principally changes viscosity level.
objections.objection: The intervention changes two modifier axes simultaneously: AC1920 is set to 15% and TK100 to 5%, while the reactive core is reduced to a reactive mass fraction of 0.8000. Although the H-CORE comparison accounts for mass dilution through the 7.61% prediction, the composition does not isolate the effects of acrylic modification from tackifier modification. Any drift suppression below 3.80% cannot be attributed to acrylic chemistry, tackifier chemistry, or their interaction separately.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The stated thresholds may produce apparent acceptance or falsification of H-CORE/H-RESIN without establishing that the difference is larger than preparation-state variability.
objections.objection: The protocol requires only two independent preparations and does not control process state, while the declared process_state_risk score is 0.75 and the E2 repeatability data show a 120 C max/min realized-viscosity ratio of 3.5688 with CV 0.5848. The catalog's 2.00% discrimination threshold is therefore not demonstrated for this novel modified composition or for SI_15_60 specifically. A result below 3.80% or at/above 7.61% across two repeats could reflect uncontrolled realization differences, and the protocol has no repeat-agreement or uncertainty criterion to rule that out.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The observable itself remains interpretable, but its threshold comparison would be less reliable than the proposal claims because repeatability and uncertainty are not quantified.
objections.objection: The primary observable SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15 is directly calculated from matched-window measurements at 15 and 60 minutes, with intermediate points recorded. It does not require a model fit, extrapolation, or imputation. No material objection applies to direct interpretability, although its uncertainty is inadequately characterized by the two-repeat protocol.

skeptic.recommended_change: Use a matched reactive-mass, factorial comparison consisting of the reactive-core condition, acrylic-only at 15%, tackifier-only at 5%, and the 15% acrylic plus 5% tackifier dual-axis condition. Apply identical 120 C hold histories with at least three independent preparations per condition, record and control the missing process-history variables, and require an explicit repeat-uncertainty or repeat-agreement rule before comparing SI_15_60 with 3.80% and 7.61%.
skeptic.strongest_objection: The stated falsification thresholds are not practically validated by the protocol: only two uncontrolled preparation repeats are required despite a process_state_risk score of 0.75 and E2 120 C realization variability of CV 0.5848 and max/min ratio 3.5688. Consequently, crossing 3.80% or 7.61% cannot be confidently interpreted as formulation-mechanism falsification.

tool_trace.name: get_state_aware_rheology_summary
tool_trace.reason: Load the upstream formulation-versus-state rheology structure, state-shift behavior, local temperature-sensitivity coordinate, and E1/E5 hold contrast before comparing candidate experiments.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The phosphoric-acid-labelled E1 +P curve is not used in the chemistry-audited primary state model.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.

provenance_audit.reason: The source record is phosphoric-acid-labelled and its additive identity/amount is not represented in formulations.csv; it is retained as sensitivity-only until chemistry is reconciled.

result.source_scope: original pre-validation local measurements with chemistry-comparability audit

result.claim_boundary: External examples are analogues. They support candidate-family and coarse-region hypotheses, not an exact optimum for AC1920/TK100 and not a proven local molecular mechanism. The current reconstruction uses only pre-result evidence at runtime; the exact validation coordinates and outcome are excluded from candidate construction, ranking and tie-breaking.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

local_reactive_core_anchor.reason: E2 is the geometric centre of the original five-point local design: 50/50 PPG2000/PDP-70 and NCO:OH=1.80, centered between E1/E3 stoichiometric perturbations and E4/E5 composition perturbations.
local_reactive_core_anchor.stoichiometry_note: The E2 NCO:OH=1.80 label applies to the original reactive core. If a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, true stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified material specifications.

stability_hypotheses.H1_formulation_family: Partial replacement of the reactive-only formulation by an acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like resin can reduce hot-hold viscosity drift under matched process conditions.
stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.
